title: Office Prom
logline: At Michael's charity Office Prom in the warehouse, Jan brings the news that Scranton survives, Dwight and Angela slow-dance 'by accident', and Jim, facing a Monday deadline on his transfer, finally tells Pam he's in love with her.
outline: A: Michael throws a charity prom while waiting for corporate's decision; Jan arrives with the news that Scranton survives, and stays for one dance. B: Jim's transfer deadline is Monday; he tells Pam in the parking lot that he loves her, she says she can't, he gives her the Christmas card, and later in the empty office they kiss. C: Ryan brings Kelly to avoid a conversation, and Dwight and Angela slow-dance 'by accident' while Oscar watches. Order: cold, A, B, A, C, B, A, B, C, A, B, tag
storySoFar: At Michael's charity Office Prom in the warehouse ('Under the Sea of Paper', proceeds to the Scranton High art program, Kevin's band Scrantonicity on stage), Jan arrived in person: Scranton survives, Stamford closes, nobody here loses their job, and she gave Michael one dance that 'never happened'. Jim learned that if Stamford closed, his transfer would become a job in Utica, due Monday. In the parking lot he told Pam he's in love with her; she said she's getting married in June and can't. He gave her the Christmas card he had kept back. She read it alone in the dark office, Jim came back, and they kissed. On Monday morning they said 'Morning' to each other and nothing was settled. Dwight and Angela slow-danced 'by accident' while Oscar watched; Ryan brought Kelly to avoid a conversation and danced with her. Pam's wedding to Roy is still set for June 10.

stateChanges.progress: Jim told Pam he loves her; she said she can't; he gave her the card; they kissed in the empty office. Unresolved.

stateChanges.status: He confessed; they kissed; she's still engaged

stateChanges.text: Jim must decide about the Utica job on Monday
Stamford is closing; some of its staff may come to Scranton

scenes.recap: Michael and Darryl decorate the warehouse for the prom; Michael explains the theme, 'Under the Sea of Paper.'

beats.caption: hangs a streamer made of blue copy paper from a forklift

beats.text: The theme is 'Under the Sea of Paper.' It's like a regular sea. But with paper. Which is what we sell.
Paper and water are kind of enemies, Michael.
So is the warehouse and the office, Darryl. And yet here we are. Decorating together.
That's... actually kind of deep.
Thank you. I got it off a mug.

scenes.recap: Corporate decides today; Jan promised to call before five. Michael stares at the phone and pretends to be calm.

beats.text: DECISION DAY
Michael, you've asked me if the phone works six times. It works.
Could you call it? From your phone? Just to check?
Jan said before five. It's eleven.

lines: Today corporate decides if we live or die. And tonight, I'm throwing a prom.
Either it's a celebration, or it's a very fun funeral. With a DJ. Darryl's the DJ.

scenes.recap: Jim gets a call from corporate: if Stamford closes, his transfer request becomes a sales job in Utica, and he has to decide by Monday.

beats.caption: takes a call from corporate HR

beats.text: Utica? If Stamford... Okay. Monday. I'll let you know Monday. Thanks.

lines: If Stamford closes, my transfer becomes a job in Utica. I have until Monday.
Monday is a really close day. It's like, right after the weekend.

beats.caption: takes a folded Christmas card out of his jacket, looks at it, puts it back

scenes.recap: The prom begins: Kevin's band Scrantonicity plays, Michael hosts, and Jan still hasn't called.

beats.text: THE OFFICE PROM

beats.caption: plays the drums for Scrantonicity, eyes closed

beats.text: Welcome to the Dunder Mifflin Office Prom! Five dollars a ticket. All proceeds go to the art program at Scranton High.
I paid five dollars to stand in the warehouse.
My first prom was in a warehouse. 1961. Raided by eleven.

scenes.recap: Ryan brings Kelly to prom 'to avoid a conversation'; Oscar watches Dwight and Angela pretend not to see each other.

beats.text: Ryan asked me to prom. Well. I asked if he was going and he said 'probably.' So, prom date.

lines: If I came with Kelly, we wouldn't have to talk about whether we're together.
We'd just... be at a prom. Together. That's a loophole. I took a class on loopholes.

beats.text: Dwight. Angela. Lovely to see you both. Separately. Very separately.
I don't know who this woman is.
Nor I him.

scenes.recap: Roy leaves for a beer run with the warehouse guys; Jim asks Pam if they can talk, outside.

beats.text: Me and the guys are doing a beer run. Back in an hour. Have fun, babe.
Hey. You came. You look nice.
Can I talk to you? Outside. For a second.
Sure.

scenes.recap: Jan walks into the prom in person: Scranton survives, Stamford closes, and nobody here loses their job.

beats.text: Jan. You came. You didn't call. Is that bad? You came in person. That's bad. That's how they do it in movies.
Michael. Scranton stays. Stamford closes. Your numbers were better. And your fax was... persuasive.
Nobody loses their job?
Nobody here.
EVERYBODY! WE'RE NOT CLOSING! I KEPT MY PROMISE! THAT I SHOULDN'T HAVE MADE!
Fine.

scenes.recap: In the parking lot Jim tells Pam he's in love with her; she says she can't. He gives her the Christmas card and goes.

beats.text: Pam. I'm in love with you.
Jim. I'm getting married. In June. You picked out the invitations.
I know. I just needed you to know. Once. Before I decide about Utica.
I can't. I'm sorry. I can't.

beats.caption: hands her the folded Christmas card

beats.text: This was supposed to be in the box. Merry Christmas. A little late.

beats.caption: Pam holds the card and doesn't open it

scenes.recap: A slow song; Dwight and Angela end up dancing 'by accident'; Kelly and Ryan dance too; Oscar sees everything.

beats.text: SLOW SONG
I seem to have been pushed into you by the crowd.
There is no crowd, Dwight.

beats.caption: pulls Ryan into a slow dance; he lets her

lines: I'm not going to tell anyone. It's more fun to know.
Also, they dance beautifully. It's infuriating.

scenes.recap: Jan stays; Michael asks her to dance, and she allows one dance that never happened.

beats.text: Jan. Would you like to dance? As a professional colleague. Professionally.
One dance. And it never happened.
What never happened?
Exactly.

beats.caption: dances with Jan to Scrantonicity, badly, beaming

lines: We saved the branch. I danced with Jan. Kevin played the drums.
Best night of my life. Again. I keep having those. That's how you know it's a family.

scenes.recap: Alone in the dark office, Pam reads the card; Jim walks back in, and they kiss.

beats.text: LATER

beats.caption: opens the Christmas card and reads it, twice

beats.text: I forgot my keys.

beats.caption: kisses her. She kisses him back.

beats.text: Jim, I...
Yeah.

scenes.recap: Monday morning: Pam is at her desk, Jim walks in, they look at each other, and Michael bursts out to greet his family. Nothing is settled.

beats.text: MONDAY
Morning.
Morning.
Good morning, Scranton! Still here! Still open! Still a family! Who wants a bagel?
